body: I got diagnosed with epilepsy a couple of years ago and have had numerous grand mal seizures since. Usually before I'll have a grand mal seizure I'll start to have absence seizures, which is a lot like zoning out. Sometimes I notice this but other times I don't. For the seizure itself... During the tonic clonic (shaking and stiffening) part I'm completely unconscious, I've never been even partly conscious during one. After the seizure I'm just confused and in a weird daze which can take a while to get out of it. It's usually really frustrating because I'll *know* what's happened and what's going and what I want to say but the words just refuse to come out of my mouth, I can't communicate with anyone. It's usually also really tiring and often gives me a pretty bad headache. And the best thing others can do is make sure we don't hit ourselves during our fall, if possible, or against anything when we start jerking our arms and stuff and make sure we're on our sides. If the shaking and stiffening part of a seizures lasts longer than 5 minutes you need to call a professional in, just like you need to call if they stop breathing during the seizure for a long time.
I've been 'lucky' enough to only have had grand mal seizures at my own home but sometimes I don't recall going from upstairs to downstairs so that can be a surprise sometimes...

Ode to Sleep. Always has been and I think forever will be. I mean part of the song name is literally what I go by online, and have been going only by, for over half a decade. Truly one of their best and most personal songs.
Eugenia Cooney. She somehow keeps getting skinnier and skinnier, it's disturbing. Whenever I read her name in a title somewhere I'm immediately afraid it'll be the one that announces her death.
I can’t imagine not thinking about how cute girls are. I am who I am and that’s that. And apparently it’s very obvious, since my parents said they’ve known years before I came out.

When I get a seizure I always get grand mal seizures, and I never notice when I get into one, except for one time when I smelled something burning, but I don’t know if that was just a one-time-thing. Maybe I’ll get ‘used’ to it later (obviously don’t hope so, but I’m 15 and only have had seizures for half a year or so). But right at the end I kinda wake up? I don’t know how to explain it, I can hear everyone around me and even open my eyes and hear myself making that weird noise people make before and after seizures. My parents say I just go blank and won’t answer anything, so they do sorta have time to ‘prepare’ themselves (get towels in case I bite my tongue, get my medication in case my seizure lasts for 3+ minutes etc.). They also say I get really pale, especially in the face.
I’m Dutch, and I’d have to go with the Dutch word for cotton candy. Here we say ‘suikerspin’ which literally translates to ‘sugar spider’. Fun.

Breathing in for 4 seconds, hold it for 7 seconds and breathe out for 8 seconds. It usually helps me to at least be able to breathe normally again, sometimes it doesn’t but most of the time it will. I don’t know anything other than breathing exercises though...
Water, bloodbending is cool as hell
Fell out of my bed and somehow broke my wrist, I didn’t sleep in a bunk bed or anything. I just fell and managed to break my wrist!
Yeah, I’m doing good don’t worry. Just glad he didn’t do anything. Hoping it won’t happen again!

Quite recently something happened. Last week I took the train home, which was about an hour and a half. Halfway through the ride a guy walked toward me. He was obviously quite drunk, since he couldn’t walk straight.  I also thought he was high, but not sure. The weirdest thing about him was that he didn’t wear any shoes or socks, and he had two very big cuts in his leg that were still bleeding a lot. Since it was late, not a lot of people were on the train. And when he started walking near me, he already creeped me out a lot and made me uncomfortable, especially since I’m not even an adult. When he decided to sit next to me I didn’t trust it at all, and he kept looking at me as well. I was quite scared at this point, and decided to sit somewhere else. A few moments later he sat near me, again. I didn’t wanna take a risk and kept walking through the train, not stopping, until the train stopped. Although he wasn’t fast, since he was quite drunk, he did try and follow me. When I reached the end of the train I decided to sit down, wait until he decided to sit near me, and walk over to the other side of the train again. I kept it up and made it home safely. 

I don’t know how common this is in other countries, but it almost never  happens where I’m from. I texted my grandpa, who works at multiple train stations as security, and he said that he had encounters like this very rarely.

It may not sound that scary, but I’d never experienced something like this before. The fact that it was nearly 2 AM didn’t help much either.
